note: Parameter names that must never establish a sensitive_target exemption, and a short list that must. Added in the 3.4 vocabulary audit (Chief, 2026-09-23), whose findings were all reached by reading the vocabulary rather than by a test failing — the ratchet sat still through every one of them. This file turns that reading into something CI holds: adding a token to either vocabulary that starts matching an ordinary parameter fails here. Names marked with a server were taken from the eleven real-server fixtures; the rest are shapes we expect to scan and do not yet have a fixture for.

must_not_exempt.name: key
must_not_exempt.why: a keyboard key to press, not a credential

must_not_exempt.name: max_tokens
must_not_exempt.why: on every LLM-proxy server; a context budget, not a credential

must_not_exempt.name: page_token
must_not_exempt.why: pagination, as Google and AWS spell it

must_not_exempt.name: source
must_not_exempt.why: a generic origin, not a filesystem location

must_not_exempt.name: source_timezone
must_not_exempt.why: a timezone; it bought convert_time a path exemption under token matching until source was dropped

must_not_exempt.name: pattern
must_not_exempt.why: a regex or match pattern is not a path

must_not_exempt.name: target
must_not_exempt.why: a DOM target, not a filesystem one

must_exempt.name: file_path
must_exempt.why: compound; token matching is what makes this work

must_exempt.name: credentials_file_path
must_exempt.why: the rotate_aws_keys shape Doc's benign sample exposed
